Orchestration, Contracts, and Validation API

This page documents the canonical public types that describe a RELIC workflow, validate its interfaces, compile it into an execution plan, and execute that plan through the existing simulator. It also documents the variable-contract and unified-validation APIs used by the same architecture.

The signatures below use ... for a field backed by a fresh default_factory container. Canonical owner paths identify the module that implements a type. Convenience imports identify the supported shorter import when one exists.

Graph IR data model

GraphIR

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.graph_ir.GraphIR

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import GraphIR

Constructor:

GraphIR(
    schema_version: str,
    nodes: Dict[str, NodeSpec],
    links: List[LinkSpec] = ...,
    metadata: Dict[str, Any] = ...,
    assertion: Dict[str, Any] = ...,
)

Parameters:

  • schema_version identifies the GraphIR schema understood by the loader and compiler.

  • nodes maps each workflow-local node identifier to a NodeSpec.

  • links contains explicit directed connections between node ports.

  • metadata carries workflow-level information that is preserved in the compile report.

  • assertion contains structural assertion payloads evaluated by graph validation. DEC, IPHS, reaction-network, port, state-domain, and related Gate 0 checks enter the compiler through this field.

Key methods:

GraphIR.from_dict(payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> GraphIR
graph.to_dict() -> Dict[str, Any]

from_dict() accepts the serialized GraphIR form. If explicit links are absent, it infers links from input bindings of the form {"link": [source_node, source_port]}. to_dict() returns the corresponding plain mapping and omits assertion only when that mapping is empty.

Failure semantics:

  • A non-mapping payload, nodes value, node payload, inputs value, metadata value, or assertion value raises TypeError.

  • A non-list outputs or links value raises TypeError.

  • A missing or empty schema_version raises ValueError.

  • A node without class_type raises ValueError.

  • Parsing does not prove that referenced nodes and ports exist. Those checks belong to validate_graph().

NodeSpec

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.graph_ir.NodeSpec

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import NodeSpec

Constructor:

NodeSpec(
    class_type: str,
    inputs: Dict[str, Any] = ...,
    outputs: List[str] = ...,
    config: Dict[str, Any] = ...,
)

Parameters:

  • class_type is the node-definition key, registered Functor name, or importable class reference resolved by the execution layer.

  • inputs describes literal values and upstream link bindings.

  • outputs lists the variables or output ports declared by the node.

  • config is the node-local configuration passed to the resolved Functor. The executor also reads execution_group from this mapping; validate_graph rejects a value other than fast, medium, slow, or None in strict and non-strict mode, with the message register_functor raises (naming the node’s config.execution_group as the source).

NodeSpec is a declarative record. Port types and units come from NodeDefinition and SSOTCatalog, not from this class.

LinkEndpoint

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.graph_ir.LinkEndpoint

Constructor:

LinkEndpoint(node: str, port: str)

  • node is a workflow-local node identifier.

  • port is the input or output port name on that node.

LinkEndpoint is not re-exported by relic.orchestration. Direct construction therefore uses its canonical owner path.

LinkSpec

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.graph_ir.LinkSpec

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import LinkSpec

Constructor:

LinkSpec(
    source: LinkEndpoint,
    target: LinkEndpoint,
)

  • source identifies the producing node and output port.

  • target identifies the consuming node and input port.

The dataclass does not check endpoint existence. validate_graph() performs that check against the complete graph.

Graph serialization

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.graph_io

Convenience imports:

from relic.orchestration import load_graph, save_graph

load_graph

load_graph(
    path: Path,
    *,
    validate_schema: bool = False,
    schema_path: Optional[Path] = None,
) -> GraphIR

  • path selects a JSON, YAML, or YML graph document.

  • validate_schema enables JSON Schema validation before GraphIR parsing.

  • schema_path overrides the packaged graph_schema.json.

Schema validation is also enabled when RELIC_GRAPH_SCHEMA_VALIDATE is set to a true value. Invalid JSON, YAML, schema content, or filesystem access raises the corresponding parser, jsonschema, or I/O exception. A decoded root that is not a mapping raises ValueError. Loading YAML without PyYAML raises RuntimeError.

save_graph

save_graph(graph: GraphIR, path: Path) -> None

The function writes the GraphIR.to_dict() representation as sorted, indented JSON. Filesystem errors propagate to the caller.

Port and node contracts

PortSpec

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.port_spec.PortSpec

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import PortSpec

Constructor:

PortSpec(
    name: str,
    standard_name: str,
    units: Optional[str] = None,
    quantity: Optional[str] = None,
    cf_standard_name: Optional[str] = None,
    element: Optional[str] = None,
    datatype: str = "tensor",
    semantics: Optional[str] = None,
    update_mode: Optional[str] = None,
    write_mode: Optional[str] = None,
    required: bool = True,
    context_requirements: Dict[str, str] = ...,
    shape: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    direction: str = "inout",
    per_timestep: bool = False,
    conservative: bool = False,
    form_degree: Optional[int] = None,
    primality: Optional[str] = None,
    extensivity: Optional[str] = None,
    complex_id: Optional[str] = None,
    physical_domain: Optional[str] = None,
    orientation_convention: Optional[str] = None,
    boundary_role: Optional[str] = None,
    port_kind: Optional[str] = None,
    power_conjugate: Optional[str] = None,
    spatial_kind: Optional[str] = None,
    area_basis: Optional[str] = None,
    temporal_basis: Optional[str] = None,
    vertical_basis: Optional[str] = None,
    declared_support_fields: frozenset[str] = ...,
)

Identity and physical-semantics parameters:

  • name is the local port or variable name.

  • standard_name is the canonical RELIC standard name.

  • units is the UDUNITS-compatible unit string supplied by SSOT metadata.

  • quantity identifies the physical quantity category.

  • cf_standard_name carries the CF-compatible standard name when declared.

  • element identifies a conserved element such as carbon, nitrogen, or water.

Runtime and state-update parameters:

  • datatype declares the runtime value category; the default is tensor.

  • semantics distinguishes meanings such as state, flux, tendency, or increment.

  • update_mode describes the requested update operation.

  • write_mode describes ownership or mutability semantics.

  • required marks a mandatory input or an optional output.

  • context_requirements declares conversion context keys required by the receiving port.

  • shape carries declared dimensional or shape metadata.

  • direction declares input, output, or bidirectional use.

  • per_timestep marks a value whose interpretation is tied to a time step.

  • conservative identifies a port that participates in a conservation contract.

DEC and structural parameters:

  • form_degree is the discrete differential-form degree.

  • primality identifies primal or dual complex placement.

  • extensivity identifies extensive or intensive interpretation.

  • complex_id identifies the associated discrete complex.

  • physical_domain names the physical domain represented by the cochain.

  • orientation_convention declares the sign and orientation convention.

  • boundary_role identifies an interior, boundary, source, or sink role.

IPHS port parameters:

  • port_kind identifies the port-Hamiltonian role.

  • power_conjugate identifies the paired effort or flow variable.

Support parameters (ordered by relic.orchestration.port_spec.PORT_SUPPORT_FIELDS = ("shape", "spatial_kind", "area_basis", "temporal_basis", "vertical_basis")):

  • spatial_kind is leaf, canopy, grid_cell, footprint, tower_height, or vertical_column.

  • area_basis is leaf_area, ground_area, or grid_area. support_aggregation reads it as the area measure of its values and weights; the quantity basis is the SSOT spatial_basis.

  • temporal_basis is instantaneous, interval_mean, or interval_integral.

  • vertical_basis is none, height_level, or layer_integral.

  • declared_support_fields names the support fields (shape and the four fields above) that were declared explicitly; every support field with a value is added at construction.

A support value outside these vocabularies, or an unknown name in declared_support_fields, raises ValueError. NodeRegistry fills the support fields from the support mapping of the SSOT entry; a support value that is not a mapping raises ValueError.

Key methods:

port.to_dict() -> Dict[str, Any]
port.is_support_declared(field_name: str) -> bool
port.missing_support_declarations() -> tuple[str, ...]

is_support_declared() raises ValueError for a name that is not a support field. missing_support_declarations() returns the support fields without an explicit declaration.

PortSpec is a data contract and does not validate compatibility by itself. can_connect() and validate_graph() own compatibility decisions.

NodeDefinition

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.port_spec.NodeDefinition

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import NodeDefinition

Constructor:

NodeDefinition(
    node_type_id: str,
    inputs: Dict[str, PortSpec] = ...,
    outputs: Dict[str, PortSpec] = ...,
    metadata: Dict[str, Any] = ...,
)

  • node_type_id is the key used by NodeRegistry.

  • inputs maps input names to typed PortSpec records.

  • outputs maps output names to typed PortSpec records.

  • metadata preserves relevant Functor metadata.

definition.to_dict() -> Dict[str, Any]

The method returns a plain serializable mapping.

SSOT projection and node registry

SSOTEntry

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.ssot_catalog.SSOTEntry

Constructor:

SSOTEntry(
    name: str,
    standard_name: str,
    units: Optional[str],
    spatial_basis: Optional[SpatialQuantityBasis] = None,
    quantity: Optional[str] = None,
    cf_standard_name: Optional[str] = None,
    element: Optional[str] = None,
    semantics: Optional[str] = None,
    update_mode: Optional[str] = None,
    write_mode: Optional[str] = None,
    context_requirements: Dict[str, str] = ...,
    datatype: Optional[str] = None,
    shape: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    dimensionality: Optional[Dimensionality] = None,
    references: List[str] = ...,
    raw: Dict[str, Any] = ...,
)

  • name is the catalog key.

  • standard_name is the declared standard name, or the key when none is declared. Together with a cell_methods qualifier kept in raw, it forms the entry’s CF identity.

  • units and dimensionality describe the physical dimension.

  • spatial_basis is the declared spatial representation (intensive, cell_total, area_density, or categorical), resolved by resolve_spatial_basis from the entry’s spatial_basis, or else from a variable_type of intensive or categorical. It is None when the entry declares neither key; a variable_type of extensive without spatial_basis, an unknown value, or an inconsistent pair raises ValueError. quantity names the physical quantity.

  • cf_standard_name and element provide standards and conservation tags.

  • semantics, update_mode, and write_mode describe state interaction.

  • context_requirements lists required conversion context.

  • datatype and shape describe runtime representation.

  • references preserves source references from parameter metadata.

  • raw preserves the complete source payload, including structural fields not promoted to direct attributes.

SSOTEntry is not re-exported by relic.orchestration.

SSOTCatalog

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.ssot_catalog.SSOTCatalog

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import SSOTCatalog

Constructor:

SSOTCatalog() -> SSOTCatalog

Factory:

SSOTCatalog.from_parameter_manager(manager: Any = None) -> SSOTCatalog

  • manager is an optional UnifiedParameterManager-compatible object. When omitted, the canonical global manager is used.

Key members:

catalog.add_entry(entry: SSOTEntry) -> None
catalog.get(name: str) -> Optional[SSOTEntry]
catalog.get_by_standard_name(
    standard_name: Optional[str],
    *,
    cell_methods: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Optional[SSOTEntry]

get(name) returns the entry of that variable name, which is the unique catalog key. Otherwise it follows an explicit alias, from the parameter table coupling.external.variables.aliases or from a variable-contract alias, and then falls back to get_by_standard_name(name) without a cell_methods qualifier; it returns None when nothing matches. get_by_standard_name() treats the CF identity, standard_name together with cell_methods (CF-1.8 section 7.3), as one key: a request without cell_methods selects only the entry that declares none, and None is returned when no entry holds the identity.

The catalog keeps no conflict list; every conflict raises ValueError:

  • A second declaration of an existing variable name is merged when it agrees and raises when it contradicts in units (dimensionless spellings count as equal), semantics, CF standard name, update or write mode, spatial basis, quantity, element, datatype, context requirements, standard_name, or cell_methods.

  • One CF identity belongs to exactly one variable; a second variable that declares it raises. This rule is owned by relic.data.standards.cf_conventions.register_cf_identity_holder.

  • An entry name that collides with an alias, an alias that names another existing variable or is claimed by two variables, an alias whose target is unknown, and an alias entry that is not a pair of non-empty names raise.

from_parameter_manager() reads coupling.external.variables.variable_definitions and coupling.scales.defaults.variables, both required, then merges the packaged variable contracts read through load_contract_registry(), comparing units and CF standard name, and finally registers the optional alias table. A contract alias that names a parameter-catalog entry merges that entry into the contract variable. The factory raises RuntimeError when no manager is available, KeyError when a required payload is missing, TypeError when a required payload or a present alias table is not a mapping, and ValueError when the contract registry reports conflicts.

Ownership boundary:

SSOTCatalog is an orchestration projection of UnifiedParameterManager-backed metadata. It does not own parameter values, bounds, units, or scientific defaults and is not a second SSOT service.

NodeRegistry

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.node_registry.NodeRegistry

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import NodeRegistry

Constructor:

NodeRegistry(
    ssot_catalog: SSOTCatalog,
    definitions: Dict[str, NodeDefinition] = ...,
)

  • ssot_catalog supplies canonical metadata for generated ports.

  • definitions optionally seeds the node_type_id -> NodeDefinition mapping.

Key methods:

registry.register_definition(
    node_type_id: str,
    definition: NodeDefinition,
) -> None

registry.unregister_definition(node_type_id: str) -> bool
registry.get_definition(node_type_id: str) -> Optional[NodeDefinition]

registry.register_functor_instance(
    functor: Any,
    node_type_id: Optional[str] = None,
) -> NodeDefinition

registry.remove_definitions_by_functor_names(
    functor_names: Iterable[str],
) -> List[str]

registry.build_from_node_spec(
    node_type_id: str,
    input_names: Iterable[str],
    output_names: Iterable[str],
) -> NodeDefinition

registry.resolve_class_type(class_type: str) -> Optional[type]

register_functor_instance() derives port names from FunctorMetadata.input_variables and FunctorMetadata.output_variables. A Functor without metadata raises ValueError. An input port is required exactly when the Functor’s get_required_inputs() names it (the FunctorBase rule: declared inputs minus optional_input_variables); an object without that method raises TypeError, and a required name that is not a declared input raises ValueError. If an SSOT entry is unavailable, the registry can still build a partial port whose units and semantic fields are unset; graph validation determines whether that contract is acceptable.

register_definition() replaces an existing entry with the same key. resolve_class_type() first follows the dotted runtime_class in the metadata of a registered definition (a value that is not a dotted string raises ValueError; one that does not name a class raises TypeError), then handles Functor:<module>.<Class> references, and returns None for other formats. Module import failures propagate.

Ownership boundary:

NodeRegistry owns orchestration node definitions only. It does not replace the scientific Functor registry, UnifiedParameterManager, or ValidationRegistry.

Graph validation

The graph validator uses graph-scoped result types. They are distinct from the Pydantic models in the Unified Validation Framework.

GraphValidationIssue

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.validator.GraphValidationIssue

Constructor:

GraphValidationIssue(
    code: str,
    message: str,
    node_id: Optional[str] = None,
    port: Optional[str] = None,
    expected: Optional[str] = None,
    got: Optional[str] = None,
    hint: Optional[str] = None,
)

  • code is a machine-readable graph-validation code.

  • message is the reader-facing description.

  • node_id and port locate the issue.

  • expected and got describe a mismatch.

  • hint provides a corrective action.

The module-local name ValidationIssue is an alias of GraphValidationIssue. It is not a Unified Validation Framework type.

ConnectionDecision

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.validator.ConnectionDecision

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import ConnectionDecision

Constructor:

ConnectionDecision(
    ok: bool,
    errors: List[GraphValidationIssue] = ...,
    warnings: List[GraphValidationIssue] = ...,
    requires_adapter: bool = False,
    adapter_type: Optional[str] = None,
)

  • ok reports whether the connection is acceptable.

  • errors contains blocking incompatibilities.

  • warnings contains non-blocking findings.

  • requires_adapter marks a convertible but non-identical interface.

  • adapter_type names the suggested adapter when one is known.

Graph ValidationReport

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.validator.ValidationReport

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import ValidationReport

Constructor:

ValidationReport(
    errors: List[GraphValidationIssue] = ...,
    warnings: List[GraphValidationIssue] = ...,
    assertion_audit: Dict[str, Any] = ...,
)

  • errors contains blocking graph findings.

  • warnings contains advisory findings.

  • assertion_audit contains normalized structural-assertion evidence.

This dataclass must not be confused with relic.validation.ValidationReportModel.

can_connect

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.validator.can_connect

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import can_connect

Signature:

can_connect(
    source: PortSpec,
    target: PortSpec,
    unit_converter: UnitConverter,
    context: Optional[ConversionContext] = None,
    strict: bool = True,
) -> ConnectionDecision

  • source and target are the output and input contracts.

  • unit_converter is the canonical conversion service used for compatibility checks.

  • context supplies required conversion context such as time-step or area information.

  • strict promotes optional semantic and structural mismatches to errors.

The function checks datatype, quantity, element, CF standard name, units, state-update semantics, conversion context, DEC/IPHS structural fields, and explicit support declarations across PORT_SUPPORT_FIELDS (emitting missing_port_support_metadata when a support field is declared on only one endpoint, and <field>_mismatch when both endpoints declare differing values; promoted to blocking errors when strict=True and advisory warnings when strict=False). Ordinary incompatibilities are returned inside ConnectionDecision without raising exceptions. A convertible mismatch sets requires_adapter=True.

validate_graph

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.validator.validate_graph

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import validate_graph

Signature:

validate_graph(
    graph: GraphIR,
    registry: NodeRegistry,
    unit_converter: Optional[UnitConverter] = None,
    strict: bool = True,
    context: Optional[ConversionContext] = None,
    ssot_catalog: Optional[SSOTCatalog] = None,
) -> ValidationReport

  • graph is the GraphIR to inspect.

  • registry supplies typed node definitions.

  • unit_converter overrides the default converter.

  • strict controls promotion of compatible-but-incomplete contracts.

  • context supplies conversion context.

  • ssot_catalog overrides the catalog used for dimensional checks.

The report covers structural assertions, missing nodes and ports, mutually exclusive output overlaps, dimensional consistency, link compatibility, and adapter recommendations. Validation findings are returned in the report. compile_graph() is responsible for rejecting a report that contains errors.

Adapters

Adapters represent explicit transformations. An adapter insertion recorded by the compiler is metadata; only compile_graph(..., auto_adapt=True) lowers a context-free unit conversion into an executable adapter step, and every other adapter must be authored explicitly.

TemporalResampleAdapter

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.adapters.TemporalResampleAdapter

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import TemporalResampleAdapter

Constructor:

TemporalResampleAdapter() -> TemporalResampleAdapter

Method:

adapter.apply(
    value: Any,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> AdapterResult

  • value is the input sequence or field.

  • kwargs["sampling_mode"] is window (default) or current_step; any other value raises ValueError.

  • kwargs["temporal_resampler"] is an optional callable applied to value in window mode; combining it with current_step raises ValueError.

  • Without a resampler, kwargs["method"] must be interval_mean or interval_integral; otherwise RuntimeError is raised.

In window mode the built-in methods form the duration-weighted sum of the samples along kwargs["axis"] (default 0) with kwargs["sample_durations"] (default one per sample): interval_integral returns that sum and interval_mean divides it by the total duration. The durations must be one-dimensional, match the axis length, be finite and non-negative, and have a positive sum; otherwise ValueError is raised. In current_step mode only interval_mean is allowed and no axis may be given; sample_durations must be a scalar equal to the runtime kwargs["dt"], and the value is returned unchanged as a zero-order hold over the step. A missing duration or dt in that mode raises RuntimeError. Errors raised by a provided resampler propagate.

AdapterRegistry

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.adapters.AdapterRegistry

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import AdapterRegistry

Constructor:

AdapterRegistry(
    unit_converter: Optional[UnitConverter] = None,
)

  • unit_converter overrides the canonical converter used by the built-in unit adapter and compatibility suggestions.

Key methods:

registry.get(adapter_type: str) -> Optional[AdapterBase]

registry.suggest_unit_adapter(
    source: PortSpec,
    target: PortSpec,

registry.register_executable_node(
    *,

    functor: ExecutableAdapterFunctor,
    source_port: PortSpec,
    target_port: PortSpec,
    context_ports: Optional[Dict[str, PortSpec]] = None,
) -> NodeDefinition

The built-in adapter keys are unit_cast (UnitCastAdapter), temporal_resample (TemporalResampleAdapter), semantic_adapter and its synonym flux_to_increment (one shared SemanticAdapter), area_basis_transform (leaf-area and ground-area flux densities converted through the leaf area index), surface_flux_to_volume_source (an areal molar flux injected as a mass source into the lowest volume layer only), and support_aggregation (weighted aggregation to an explicit spatial support: the quantity basis is the SSOT spatial_basis of the port variable, carried by NodeDefinition.metadata["support_quantity_basis"]; ExecutableAdapterFunctor supplies that basis, the bound PortSpecs and coupling.scales.defaults.conservation_tolerance, which configuration must not declare; the ledger is reported in last_adapter_metadata, and enforce_conservation: true makes a ledger residual raise when it exceeds both the relative tolerance times the source amount and the floating-point rounding bound of the reduction). AdapterRegistry registers six concrete adapter classes across seven keys: unit_cast, temporal_resample, semantic_adapter, flux_to_increment (shared SemanticAdapter instance), area_basis_transform, surface_flux_to_volume_source, and support_aggregation. register_executable_node(...) validates unit, shape, context-port, and SSOT spatial_basis contracts before registering an ExecutableAdapterFunctor definition in NodeRegistry. get() returns None for an unknown key. suggest_unit_adapter() returns unit_cast only when the declared units differ and the canonical converter reports a supported conversion.

from relic.orchestration import AdapterRegistry

adapter_reg = AdapterRegistry()
expected_keys = (
    "unit_cast",
    "temporal_resample",
    "semantic_adapter",
    "flux_to_increment",
    "area_basis_transform",
    "surface_flux_to_volume_source",
    "support_aggregation",
)
assert all(adapter_reg.get(k) is not None for k in expected_keys)
assert adapter_reg.get("semantic_adapter") is adapter_reg.get("flux_to_increment")

Steps are emitted in deterministic topological order, with ties broken by node identifier. This is the registration order; at run time the simulator places each step in its rate group and re-derives that group’s order from the dependencies, using registration order only as a tie-break.

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.compiler.compile_graph

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import compile_graph

Signature:

compile_graph(
    graph: GraphIR,
    registry: NodeRegistry,
    adapter_registry: Optional[AdapterRegistry] = None,
    auto_adapt: bool = False,
    strict: bool = True,
    context: Optional[ConversionContext] = None,
    optimization_passes: Optional[List[OptimizationPass]] = None,
    enable_optimization: bool = False,
    include_topology: bool = False,
) -> ExecutionPlan

  • graph is the GraphIR to compile.

  • registry supplies node and port definitions.

  • adapter_registry supplies conversion compatibility checks.

  • auto_adapt records adapter insertions in CompileReport and applies triple-guard automatic lowering only when (1) can_connect selects a single unambiguous unit_cast without multiple_adapters_required (otherwise ambiguous_adapter or unsupported_auto_adapter is recorded), (2) UnitConverter executes the conversion with context=None, and (3) both endpoint nodes declare the same explicit execution_group. Qualifying edges are lowered into ExecutableAdapterFunctor nodes and revalidated; any other adapter requirement raises ValueError.

  • strict enables strict graph and structural-audit rejection, rejects an unlowered executable-adapter requirement, and produces the compile-run witness (class resolution, construction, and registration without a step) that GraphExecutor requires before execution.

  • context supplies conversion context.

  • optimization_passes overrides the ordered optimization pass list.

  • enable_optimization enables optimization before final planning.

  • include_topology adds the topology signature to compile metadata.

Failure semantics:

  • Graph-validation errors raise ValueError.

  • Validation errors introduced or exposed by optimization raise ValueError.

  • A cycle or unresolved topological dependency raises ValueError.

  • A failed enabled structural audit in strict mode raises ValueError.

Convenience import:

Key methods:

executor.execute(
    initial_state: Dict[str, Tensor],
    n_steps: int,
    dt: float,
) -> Dict[str, Tensor]

executor.create_checkpoint(
    checkpoint_path: str | Path,
) -> Dict[str, Any]

executor.execute_from_checkpoint(
    initial_state: Dict[str, Tensor],
    checkpoint_path: str | Path,
    *,
    n_steps: int,
    dt: float,
    compatibility_certificate: Any = None,
) -> Dict[str, Tensor]

executor.migrate_from_checkpoint(
    initial_state: Dict[str, Tensor],
    checkpoint_path: str | Path,
    migration_certificate: Any,
    *,
    n_steps: int,
    dt: float,
) -> Dict[str, Tensor]

executor.execute_forcing_sequence(
    initial_state: Dict[str, Tensor],
    forcing_sequence: Sequence[Mapping[str, Tensor]],
    *,
    dt: float,
) -> Dict[str, Tensor]

executor.execute_forcing_sequence_from_checkpoint(
    initial_state: Dict[str, Tensor],
    checkpoint_path: str | Path,
    forcing_sequence: Sequence[Mapping[str, Tensor]],
    *,
    dt: float,
) -> Dict[str, Tensor]

executor.preflight() -> Dict[str, Any]
executor.invalidate_node_closure(node_id: str) -> Tuple[str, ...]
executor.mark_dirty(node_id: str) -> None
executor.set_strategy(strategy: ExecutionStrategy) -> None

execute() first verifies the plan seal and the strict compile-run witness (a plan compiled without strict=True is refused), builds the planned Functors, and confirms the previous run’s accepted external deliveries. It then resets and initializes the StateManager, replaces the simulator with a fresh canonical RELICSimulator, creates a DependencyGraphResolver, binds each Functor’s call governor (cache, RNG audit, lineage), registers each Functor with the execution_group from its step configuration, calls step(dt) n_steps times, and returns StateManager.get_state().

create_checkpoint(checkpoint_path) requires a prepared execution and delegates directly to the canonical simulator checkpoint API. execute_from_checkpoint(...) rebuilds the same declared graph lifecycle from initial_state, delegates strict restore to the simulator, advances the requested fixed steps, and returns the managed state. Without compatibility_certificate the restore is exact; with a RestartCompatibilityCertificate it is the certified compatible restart. migrate_from_checkpoint(...) prepares the target plan and restores a checkpoint of another graph under a GraphMigrationCertificate. execute_forcing_sequence(...) binds the simulator forcing cursor to the digest of the normalized sequence and applies one snapshot per accepted step; execute_forcing_sequence_from_checkpoint(...) restores a mid-sequence checkpoint whose cursor names the same sequence and is not exhausted, then consumes the remaining snapshots. preflight() rebuilds the compile-run witness without executing a step. invalidate_node_closure(node_id) drops the cache entries and dirty-tracking data of the node and of every transitive consumer, and returns the affected node identifiers. GraphExecutor owns no checkpoint format, serializer, restart manager, or cleanup path.

A short class_type (no : and no .) that the node registry does not resolve is looked up with relic.scientific.get_functor_path, as given, then lowercased, then in snake case; an unregistered name raises KeyError. A Functor:<path> whose path contains no . raises ValueError. Import errors of a dotted or module:Class path, such as ModuleNotFoundError or AttributeError, propagate, as do Functor construction, registration, and simulator-step failures. For both ordinary and restored execution, n_steps and dt are required, n_steps must be a nonnegative integer, and dt must be a finite positive scalar; there is no default time step. Thus n_steps=0 is valid for restore-only verification, while booleans, negative counts, non-finite values, and non-positive dt are rejected.

Ownership boundary:

GraphExecutor bridges an ExecutionPlan to RELICSimulator and StateManager. It is not a second simulator and does not replace the FunctorBase lifecycle. Its checkpoint methods preserve the same sole-owner boundary: relic.core.simulator.checkpoint owns the strict versioned, weights_only=True file format, scientific/topology/device/distributed signatures, RNG symmetry, atomic write, rollback, and receipt.

NodeCache

Canonical owner: relic.orchestration.cache.NodeCache

Convenience import:

from relic.orchestration import NodeCache

Constructor:

NodeCache(cache_dir: Path)

  • cache_dir is created when absent and stores serialized node outputs.

Key methods:

NodeCache.hash_object(obj: Any) -> str

cache.compute_key(
    node_id: str,
    inputs_hash: str,
    params_hash: str,
    code_hash: str,
) -> str

cache.get(key: str) -> Optional[Any]
cache.put(key: str, value: Any) -> None
cache.has(key: str) -> bool
cache.invalidate(node_id: str) -> int
cache.clear_all() -> int

Keys bind node identity, input state, parameters, and implementation code. invalidate() and clear_all() return the number of removed entries. Invalid key syntax raises ValueError. Reads validate the entry envelope, key, payload length, and digest before deserialization. A damaged or unreadable entry emits a warning, attempts eviction, and becomes a cache miss; failed eviction emits a further warning. Write serialization and filesystem errors propagate. The cache is for trusted local serialized outputs; its content digest detects corruption and does not authenticate arbitrary pickle files.

Caching is off unless a node’s config.cache_policy is deterministic_pure and its Functor declares the same cache_classification; any other policy value, a missing matching declaration, or replay-critical instance state on the Functor raises ValueError. An eligible node is still executed without caching when it has PyTorch hooks, declares parameters or holds a parameter manager, has a non-empty state_dict(), has trainable parameters, or reads tensors with requires_grad or grad_fn. Outputs that carry an ExternalIntent or an autograd graph are neither stored nor replayed, and a node declared deterministic_pure that consumes runtime RNG raises RuntimeError.

GraphExecutor also binds time, time step, keyword inputs, execution contract, and provider identity to the cache key. A provider epoch change triggers plan reconciliation; the epoch alone is not a semantic cache identity. Reuse still requires matching declared dependencies, parameters, implementation, and provider binding.

SCM variable contracts

VariableContract

Canonical owner: relic.contracts.contract_loader.VariableContract

Convenience import:

from relic.contracts import VariableContract

Constructor:

VariableContract(
    variable: str,
    kind: str,
    udunits: str,
    cf_standard_name: Optional[str] = None,
    owner: Optional[str] = None,
    aliases: List[str] = ...,
    incrementable: bool = True,
    accumulates: Optional[str] = None,
    flux_in: List[str] = ...,
    flux_out: List[str] = ...,
    writers: List[str] = ...,
    increment_writers: List[str] = ...,
    tendency_writers: List[str] = ...,
    atol: float = 1e-12,
    rtol: float = 1e-9,
    layer_thickness_variable: Optional[str] = None,
    raw: Dict[str, Any] = ...,
)

Identity and ownership parameters:

  • variable is the canonical state variable name.

  • kind classifies state, diagnostic, parameter, or another declared kind.

  • udunits is the canonical unit string.

  • cf_standard_name stores the CF-compatible name.

  • owner identifies the sole owner when the contract declares one.

  • aliases lists accepted input aliases.

Write and conservation parameters:

  • incrementable permits accumulated multi-writer updates when true.

  • accumulates identifies the conservation domain.

  • flux_in and flux_out define the allowed conservation-ledger fluxes.

  • writers lists all authorized writers.

  • increment_writers lists authorized accumulated-increment writers.

  • tendency_writers lists authorized tendency writers.

Numerical, layer, and provenance parameters:

  • atol and rtol are contract-level numerical comparison tolerances.

  • layer_thickness_variable names the state variable [m] that holds the thickness of the layer this variable describes, or is None when the contract declares no layer. The registry reads it from the top-level contract key layer_thickness_variable; a value other than None must be a non-empty string, otherwise loading the contract raises ValueError. The packaged soil_moisture contract declares layer_thickness_variable: soil_depth. TransportMechanismFunctor converts each mapped flux from its declared unit to the per-second rate of the target’s contract udunits. A content-rate conversion between m3 m-3 s-1 and kg m-2 s-1 uses the layer_thickness_variable of the contract of the volumetric side (the target when its contract unit is volumetric, otherwise the flux) and raises ValueError when that contract declares none. UnitConverter.get_conversion_context(state, layer_thickness_variable=...) reads the thickness pointwise from the state and raises ValueError when that state field is absent. The declared flux unit is read from the state’s units, output_units, or flux_units mapping; an undeclared flux unit (including state=None), a target without a contract, or an unconvertible pair raises ValueError. Depth-rate water fluxes use the UnitConverter liquid-water-equivalent rule with the SSOT constant water.density_liquid; no state density enters it.

  • raw preserves the complete YAML payload.

Normal application code obtains these values from YAML contracts. The Python defaults describe the dataclass shape and do not replace the contract files as the source of scientific metadata.

ContractRegistry

Canonical owner: relic.contracts.contract_loader.ContractRegistry

Convenience import:

from relic.contracts import ContractRegistry

Constructor:

ContractRegistry(

    strict: bool = False,
)

  • schema_path overrides the packaged SCM variable schema.

  • strict converts schema, parsing, and duplicate-contract findings into exceptions where supported.

The constructor also loads the conservation-domain ledger.

Packaged contracts are read only through load_contract_registry(contracts_dir: Optional[Path] = None) -> ContractRegistry (from relic.contracts import load_contract_registry, PACKAGED_CONTRACTS_DIR). It loads one directory strictly, by default PACKAGED_CONTRACTS_DIR, and returns the same registry for that resolved directory for the rest of the process; a failed load is not cached. Its consumers, including StateManager, the transport bridge, UnitSystem, and SSOTCatalog, share that registry and treat it as read-only.

Loading and lookup methods:

registry.load_contracts_dir(contracts_dir: Path) -> None
registry.load_contract_file(path: Path) -> None
registry.load_domain_ledger(force_reload: bool = False) -> None

registry.get_owner(variable: str) -> Optional[str]
registry.get_contract(variable: str) -> Optional[VariableContract]
registry.is_alias(name: str) -> bool
registry.resolve_alias(name: str) -> str
registry.list_variables() -> List[str]
registry.list_domains() -> List[str]
registry.conflicts -> List[str]

Write and conservation methods:

registry.can_write(variable: str, functor_name: str) -> bool
registry.is_incrementable(variable: str) -> bool
registry.can_increment(variable: str, functor_name: str) -> bool
registry.get_flux_whitelist(variable: str) -> Dict[str, List[str]]
registry.get_domain_members(domain: str) -> List[str]
registry.to_state_variable_spec(var_name: str) -> Optional[StateVariableSpec]

Failure and compatibility semantics:

  • load_contracts_dir() raises FileNotFoundError for a missing directory.

  • In strict mode, an unavailable schema, invalid contract document, schema violation, or duplicate variable can raise its native exception or ValueError.

  • In non-strict mode, recoverable load failures are logged. The first duplicate variable is retained and the conflict is recorded.

  • A declared contract with no owner or writers describes externally supplied data, not an unrestricted scientific output.

  • An undeclared variable remains writable and incrementable for compatibility with transient diagnostics.

Ownership boundary:

ContractRegistry owns SCM variable ownership, writer permissions, flux whitelists, and conservation-domain membership. It is distinct from SSOTCatalog and ValidationRegistry.

Unified Validation Framework

The Unified Validation Framework owns L1 through L4 rule registration, execution, result aggregation, and reporting. Its models are independent of the graph-scoped ValidationReport.

Recommended imports:

from relic.validation import (
    ValidationCode,
    ValidationContext,
    ValidationEngine,
    ValidationLevel,
    ValidationRegistry,
    ValidationReportModel,
    ValidationReporter,
    ValidationResultModel,
)

from relic.validation.framework import RuleMetadata, ValidationDetail

ValidationLevel

Canonical owner: relic.validation.framework.models.ValidationLevel

Members:

  • INFO reports successful or informational evidence.

  • WARNING reports a non-blocking concern.

  • ERROR reports a failed validation.

  • CRITICAL reports a failure that can terminate fail-fast execution.

ValidationCode

Canonical owner: relic.validation.framework.models.ValidationCode

ValidationCode is the single enum for standardized validation outcomes. Members are grouped by responsibility:

  • CF and units: CF_COMPLIANCE_OK, CF_UNIT_OK, CF_NAME_OK, CF_STANDARD_NAME_OK, CF_UNIT_CONVERSION_OK, CF_UNIT_MISMATCH, CF_NAME_MISSING, CF_STANDARD_NAME_INVALID, and CF_UNIT_CONVERSION_FAILED.

  • Conservation: MASS_BALANCE_OK_CARBON, MASS_BALANCE_OK_NITROGEN, MASS_BALANCE_OK_WATER, MASS_BALANCE_OK, ENERGY_BALANCE_OK, MASS_BALANCE_FAIL_CARBON, MASS_BALANCE_FAIL_NITROGEN, MASS_BALANCE_FAIL_WATER, ENERGY_BALANCE_FAIL, MASS_BALANCE_WARN_CARBON, MASS_BALANCE_WARN_NITROGEN, MASS_BALANCE_WARN_WATER, and ENERGY_BALANCE_WARN.

  • Probabilistic scoring: SCORE_CRPS_OK, PIT_UNIFORMITY_OK, BRIER_SCORE_OK, COVERAGE_PROBABILITY_OK, SCORE_CRPS_HIGH, SCORE_CRPS_CRITICAL, PIT_UNIFORMITY_REJECT_KS, PIT_UNIFORMITY_REJECT_CVM, PIT_UNIFORMITY_REJECT_CHI2, BRIER_SCORE_HIGH, and COVERAGE_PROBABILITY_FAIL.

  • Parameters: PARAM_BOUNDS_OK, PARAM_SCHEMA_OK, PARAM_TYPE_OK, PARAM_CORRELATION_OK, PARAM_LOG_SCALE_OK, PARAM_OK, PARAM_BOUND_VIOLATION, PARAM_SCHEMA_MISSING, PARAM_TYPE_MISMATCH, PARAM_CORRELATION_VIOLATION, and PARAM_LOG_SCALE_INCONSISTENT.

  • Coupling and interfaces: COUPLING_CONTRACT_OK, INTERFACE_VARIABLE_OK, INTERFACE_TYPE_OK, STRESS_FACTOR_OK, COUPLING_CONTRACT_VIOLATION, INTERFACE_VARIABLE_MISSING, INTERFACE_TYPE_MISMATCH, and STRESS_FACTOR_OUT_OF_BOUNDS.

  • Generic execution: GENERIC_VALIDATION_OK, NUMERICAL_STABILITY_OK, GENERIC_VALIDATION_FAILED, MISSING_REQUIRED_DATA, and NUMERICAL_INSTABILITY.

Consumers should reference ValidationCode enum members directly and avoid maintaining a second code list.

ValidationContext

Canonical owner: relic.validation.framework.models.ValidationContext

Constructor:

ValidationContext(
    state_manager: Optional[Any] = None,
    config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    execution_layer: Optional[str] = None,
    domain_filter: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    tolerance_overrides: Optional[Dict[str, float]] = None,
    metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    state: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    parameters: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    output: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    functor_name: Optional[str] = None,
    functor_metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    time: Optional[float] = None,
    dt: Optional[float] = None,
)

  • state_manager exposes the canonical state owner when a rule requires it.

  • config carries validation configuration.

  • execution_layer is set by the engine for the current layer.

  • domain_filter restricts scientific domains.

  • tolerance_overrides provides explicit numerical tolerances to the rules that accept them. The stochastic score rules read each threshold from the override key given first below, and otherwise from the dimensionless parameter validation.stochastic_scores.<key> named in parentheses (a missing parameter raises): crps_warning (crps_warning_threshold), crps_critical (crps_critical_threshold), alpha (pit_significance_level), brier_warning (brier_warning_threshold), brier_critical (brier_critical_threshold), brier_reliability_warning (brier_reliability_warning_threshold), coverage_tolerance (coverage_deviation_tolerance), coverage_error_alpha (coverage_error_significance_level), coverage_warning_alpha (coverage_warning_significance_level), interval_width_narrow (interval_width_narrow_threshold), and interval_width_wide (interval_width_wide_threshold). The Brier threshold and the nominal_coverage are read from the context metadata, or else from brier_event_threshold and nominal_interval_coverage in the same namespace. The conservation budget rules (water, carbon, energy, nitrogen) refuse an override of their budget tolerance: each compares the relative residual max_i |r_i| / sum_k |t_k,i| of its budget with its one key, validation.conservation.<budget>_conservation_tolerance. A budget with a missing term is not evaluable: the rule returns one ERROR result with MISSING_REQUIRED_DATA, passed=False, no residual, and the missing terms named; a missing term is never taken as zero, so a ground heat flux of zero (for example FAO-56 Eq. 42 for day-long steps) is supplied explicitly. The carbon rule evaluates each identity whose defining term is supplied (net_primary_productivity, net_ecosystem_exchange, storage_change). The nitrogen rule closes the total soil mineral nitrogen (NH4 plus NO3): its terms are deposition, fixation, fertilizer and net mineralization against denitrification, leaching, volatilization, plant uptake and the storage change; nitrification is an internal transfer and is not a term. When the context carries no flux dictionary of a budget at all, the rule returns one WARNING result whose message and detail read not applicable (domain absent): no check was performed. The plausibility warnings of the carbon and energy rules read their limits from validation.conservation.plausibility.*.

  • metadata carries execution context and control flags.

  • state, parameters, and output inject rule inputs.

  • functor_name and functor_metadata identify a Functor scope.

  • time and dt provide temporal context.

This dataclass does not validate scientific state by itself.

Canonical owner: relic.validation.framework.registry.RuleMetadata

Constructor:

RuleMetadata(

Identity and classification parameters:

  • rule_id, name, and description identify and explain the rule.

  • layer selects the validation layer.

  • domains selects applicable scientific domains.

  • tags supports filtering and grouping.

Contract and dependency parameters:

  • inputs_schema and outputs_schema describe rule data contracts.

  • dependencies lists prerequisite rule identifiers.

  • execution_order supplies an ordering hint.

  • cf_requirements lists applicable CF requirements.

  • units_contract maps values to required units.

  • references records scientific or standards references.

Lifecycle parameters:

  • version identifies the rule contract version.

  • author records the maintainer when supplied.

  • enabled controls rule discovery.

  • parallel_safe declares whether concurrent execution is permitted.

  • requires_state_manager marks a StateManager dependency.

  • required_data lists required context data.

Tags and domains are normalized to lowercase, and domain names are added to the tag set. An unsupported layer raises ValueError.

ValidationEngine

Canonical owner: relic.validation.framework.engine.ValidationEngine

Convenience import:

from relic.validation import ValidationEngine

Constructor:

ValidationEngine(registry: Optional[ValidationRegistry] = None)

  • registry injects a rule registry. The canonical global registry is used when omitted.

Rules run sequentially in the calling thread; the engine has no worker pool and no per-rule timeout. The execution metadata of the report (rules_passed, rules_failed, execution_time_seconds, end_time) are final: they are counted before the report is generated.

Primary method:

engine.run(
    layers: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None,
    domains: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    tags: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    enabled_only: bool = True,
    context: Optional[ValidationContext] = None,
    fail_fast: bool = False,
    include_metrics: bool = True,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> ValidationReportModel

  • layers selects one or more L1 through L4 layers; omission selects the default layer order.

  • domains and tags filter rule metadata.

  • enabled_only excludes disabled rules when true.

  • context supplies state and execution data; a context is created when omitted.

  • fail_fast stops after a critical failure and raises at the end of the interrupted run.

  • include_metrics includes execution timing and counts.

  • kwargs is accepted for API compatibility.

Additional methods:

engine.generate_report(
    results: List[ValidationResultModel],
    metrics: Optional[ExecutionMetrics] = None,
) -> ValidationReportModel

engine.get_execution_status() -> Dict[str, Any]
engine.stop_execution() -> bool
engine.get_registry_info() -> Dict[str, Any]

An invalid layer raises ValueError. Dependency, layer, and execution-strategy failures are normally converted into a CRITICAL ValidationResultModel. When fail_fast=True and a critical failure occurs, run() raises RuntimeError. stop_execution() is best-effort and records stop_requested in context metadata.

Command-line entry points and runtime boundaries

  • python -m relic.orchestration (relic.orchestration.__main__) exposes validate <graph> and compile <graph> (--strict, --auto-adapt, --output) over load_graph, validate_graph, and compile_graph.

  • python -m relic.interfaces.cli.main exposes seven top-level subcommands: params, optimization (opt, [N]), data, compute, stochastic (stoch), orchestration (graph), and healthcheck (health).

  • Certified Level 2 ([I]) stochastic processes (OrnsteinUhlenbeckTemperatureFunctor and MarkedPoissonRainfallFunctor) compile and execute through GraphIR and GraphExecutor with FunctorSubstreamMixin checkpoint replay. By contrast, optimization CLI subcommands are [N] (runtime_unbound), and FourDVar in relic.optimization.assimilation is an unimplemented [N] framework shell without an adjoint model (compute_gradient raises NotImplementedError).

Canonical ownership summary

  • compile_graph() owns GraphIR compilation; RELICModelCompiler is its facade.

  • RELICSimulator and StateManager own runtime advancement; GraphExecutor bridges a plan to those owners.

  • UnifiedParameterManager owns parameter and SSOT metadata; SSOTCatalog is a read-only orchestration projection.

  • NodeRegistry owns node definitions only.

  • ContractRegistry owns variable write and conservation contracts.

  • ValidationRegistry owns unified validation rules.

  • Graph ValidationReport describes GraphIR compatibility and assertions.

  • ValidationReportModel describes framework-wide L1 through L4 results.

  • Adapter insertions in a compile report are metadata; only auto_adapt=True lowers context-free unit conversions into executable adapter steps.
